source: City of Ottawa VRF_Scorecard_MVP — Value Category_Definitions.csv

categories.name: Improved Service Delivery
categories.definition: Improved Service Delivery measures the impact of initiatives that enhance the speed, reliability, accessibility, and overall quality of services provided to residents and internal customers. This includes faster response and resolution times, improved service consistency, clearer communication, reduced escalations or complaints, and more seamless end?to?end service journeys. Value is realized when an initiative improves service outcomes, strengthens customer trust and satisfaction, increases predictability of service performance, or reduces friction in interactions-resulting in a more responsive, transparent, and user?centered service experience.

categories.name: Capacity Creation
categories.definition: Capacity Creation captures the value generated by freeing up employee time and organizational capacity through the elimination, reduction, or automation of manual, repetitive, or low?value activities. This includes streamlining workflows, reducing handoffs, improving process reliability, and enabling staff to redirect effort toward higher?value, strategic, or resident?facing work. Value is realized when an initiative measurably reduces effort or cycle time, increases throughput without additional staffing, or creates reusable capacity-typically quantified in hours saved, productivity gains, or increased workload absorption-without compromising service quality.

categories.name: Direct Cost Savings
categories.definition: Direct Cost Savings reflects the tangible financial impact of initiatives that reduce current operating costs or prevent future expenditures. This includes targeted reductions in labor costs, vendor or contract spend, infrastructure and licensing expenses, rework, overtime, or other avoidable operational costs. Value is realized when an initiative delivers measurable, attributable financial benefits-such as budget reductions, avoided cost growth, or deferred spend-expressed in dollar terms. Cost savings may occur independently or as a direct outcome of improvements in capacity creation, service delivery, or risk reduction.
